rv.q: Godinez has shaved it down to its essence and made its Cuban setting both immensely vivid, specific and universal.
In all, this is one fascinating and enthralling version of Shakespeare, filled with contemporary ideas, that will certainly appeal to everyone.
MEASURE FOR MEASURE is moment by moment innovative. Godinez's storytelling is robust. And his ensemble is first-rate.
Henry Godinez's streamlined (about 100 intermissionless minutes) and vibrant production at Chicago Shakespeare comes pretty damn close.
For those who are Shakespeare fans but aren't in the mood for one of his three hour dramas or history plays, this 100-minute Measure for Measure might be the one for you.
Both Adam Poss and Cruz Gonzalez-Cadel gave more the impression of reading, and not quite convincingly at that.
